annotation.authors_or_issuer: Associate Professor of Civil Law, College of Law, University of Bahrain
key_provisions_or_claims: Robots could be treated as persons, things, animals, or a sui generis entity for liability purposes.
Bahraini Civil Code Article 175(b) on things requiring special care may cover robots as mechanical machines, making their guardian liable.
Proposes mandatory insurance for robot users covering all damage.
Proposes regulating robot manufacture and use before circulation in the state.
Proposes adding to Article 175 a joint liability of AI maker and programmer, plus a black-box mechanism to trace harmful AI acts.
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Lecture-style excerpt by a University of Bahrain civil law professor on civil liability for harm caused by robots. It reviews treating robots as persons, things (Bahraini Civil Code Art. 175), animals, or a special entity, and proposes mandatory insurance, pre-market regulation, joint maker/programmer liability, and a black-box mechanism.
